title: Astrid and the Parish
premise: Ulyana Ravensworth, concierge at the Hotel Meridian in the coastal town of Parish, has built her career on noticing what guests try to hide. A nervous stranger named Corwin pays a month's advance to hire her not to prevent a murder but to prove one hasn't happened yet — the predicted killing of Aldous Vane, Parish's beloved patriarch, at his anniversary dinner. As Ulyana investigates, she discovers the town's founding families have spent decades concealing the death of a witness, Sera Ilves, whose testimony once threatened them all; everyone insists Sera is dead, yet someone keeps leaving fresh flowers on an unmarked grave. Ulyana finds Sera alive, hidden in plain sight as the hotel's night cleaner, and realizes Corwin is Sera's son, engineered the 'prediction' to force the truth into the open before the town could silence her again. At the anniversary dinner, Ulyana exposes the conspiracy publicly, choosing justice outside the law over the tidy discretion of her filing cabinets — and finally claims a belonging she never let herself want.
about_author: Tamsin Joubert is a former small-town archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's secrets before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about quiet observers and the towns that depend on their silence.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. We meet her system: index cards on every guest of the Hotel Meridian, filed by telltale detail rather than name. Establishes Parish's rhythm and her proud isolation. When a guest checks in under a false name wearing another man's coat, she files him too. Emotional beat: competence as armor.

chapters.title: Payment in Advance
chapters.summary: Corwin Ashe hires Ulyana for an impossible job: prove that Aldous Vane will NOT be murdered at his upcoming anniversary dinner. He pays a month upfront, refuses to explain how he knows. Ulyana accepts partly from curiosity, partly because the money is too clean to refuse. Beat: unease dressed as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Vane Anniversary
chapters.summary: Ulyana surveys the Vane estate under pretext of arranging accommodations for the dinner's out-of-town guests. The family is polished and cold; Aldous himself seems oddly resigned. She notices fresh lilies on an unmarked grave in the churchyard — flowers with no card. Beat: first crack in the town's facade.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Digging through the parish records office, Ulyana finds the story of Sera Ilves, a witness who testified twenty-five years ago against the founding families and died — officially — in an accident weeks later. The file has been thumbed soft by many hands. Beat: the past pressing through the paper.

chapters.title: A Guest Who Checks Out Backwards
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. His fear and guilt surface: he knows more than he's said, and he's watching Ulyana as much as hiring her. He burns a letter in his room's sink; she logs the ash smell without confronting him. Beat: trust beginning to curdle.

chapters.title: Threats, Politely Worded
chapters.summary: Ulyana receives a note suggesting she take a holiday until after the dinner. That evening, her index-card cabinet has been searched — carefully, alphabetically. Someone who understands systems is warning her off. Beat: the hunter realizing she's also prey.

chapters.title: The Night Cleaner
chapters.summary: Working late, Ulyana observes the hotel's night cleaner, a silent woman called Mrs. Pell, moving through the lobby with uncanny familiarity — pausing where the old registry once stood, avoiding the fourth stair that creaks. Ulyana begins a new file. Beat: recognition without proof.

chapters.title: Dinner Reservations
chapters.summary: Ulyana interviews the Vane family's staff and learns the anniversary dinner seating chart places every founding-family heir at one table — and leaves one chair empty, as it has for twenty-five years. Aldous requests the empty chair be set anyway. Beat: ritual as confession.

chapters.title: What the Flowers Cost
chapters.summary: Ulyana stakes out the grave and catches the florist's delivery boy, who admits he's paid anonymously, weekly, for years — cash left in a church donation box. The handwriting on the payment notes matches a signature in the old trial transcript. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Corwin Breaks Ranks
chapters.summary: Cornered by Ulyana, Corwin admits he believes Sera Ilves is alive — and that she is his mother. He engineered the murder 'prediction' knowing Ulyana's curiosity would do what his direct questions couldn't. She feels used, then understands it. Beat: betrayal folding into alliance.

chapters.title: The Fourth Stair
chapters.summary: Ulyana sets a trap: she loosens the fourth stair's board and waits. Mrs. Pell steps over it perfectly — again. Confronted, the woman says nothing, but leaves behind a cleaning rag embroidered with initials: S.I. Beat: the dead woman three feet away.

chapters.title: Twenty-Five Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Sera's POV, brief and restrained. Her history: what she witnessed as a young housekeeper, what the families did to bury her testimony, why she chose erasure over safety, and why she cleans the hotel where it all began. Beat: grief worn as invisibility.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Approaches
chapters.summary: With six days left, Ulyana maps the conspiracy: four families, one forged accident report, one judge now retired with a lake house bought in cash. But the families have noticed her digging, and Corwin has gone missing. Beat: the net tightening.

chapters.title: Missing Person, Unreported
chapters.summary: Ulyana searches for Corwin and finds his room scrubbed professionally clean — hotel-grade work. Someone inside the Meridian is protecting the families. Her suspect list shrinks to three colleagues she's trusted for years. Beat: isolation deepening.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair Explained
chapters.summary: Ulyana confronts Aldous Vane privately. He confesses the dinner's true purpose: each year he sets the chair to dare the others to admit what they did. He believes Sera lives and wants, before he dies, to say her name aloud. Beat: an old man's penance.

chapters.title: A File Nobody Asked For
chapters.summary: Ulyana compiles everything — transcripts, flower receipts, the embroidery, the seating charts — into a single dossier. Then she finds evidence the families plan to make Sera's death official this time, timed to the dinner. Beat: the clock becoming a blade.

chapters.title: Where They Keep Corwin
chapters.summary: Following the florist lead, Ulyana traces Corwin to a boathouse owned by the retired judge. He's alive, held as insurance against Sera surfacing. She photographs everything instead of intervening — the hardest discipline of her life. Beat: patience as courage.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Sera finally speak face to face. Sera refuses to run but agrees to appear — if Ulyana can guarantee the town listens. Ulyana must decide whether to hand her dossier to the police, who may be compromised, or to the dinner table itself. Beat: the choice between law and justice.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Climax. Ulyana serves the dinner herself, in uniform, invisible. As toasts rise, she seats Sera Ilves in the empty chair. The room stops. Ulyana reads the truth aloud — names, dates, the forged report — while the families realize escape routes are sealed: press invited, documents copied, Corwin freed. Beat: silence breaking like glass.

chapters.title: What Justice Looks Like Ungoverned
chapters.summary: Aftermath begins. The police, forced by publicity, reopen the case; arrests follow, though some guilty men die free of legal consequence — and Ulyana accepts that imperfect arithmetic. Sera testifies. Corwin reconciles with his mother across a hotel breakfast table. Beat: justice as process, not verdict.

chapters.title: Resignation Letter, Unsigned
chapters.summary: Ulyana considers burning her index cards — the whole alphabetized town — and starting clean. Instead she refiles them under a new heading: witnesses, not secrets. The Meridian offers her a partnership; the town offers her something rarer, a place in it. Beat: armor set down.

chapters.title: Fresh Lilies, Signed
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Ulyana's POV. One year later, the unmarked grave bears a stone: Sera Ilves, living donor of its flowers no longer needed. Ulyana greets a nervous new guest who thinks no one notices anything — and smiles, filing the first card of a kinder archive. Beat: belonging, finally claimed.
